editorial:
Four years after the events of 2018, Laurie Strode has finally decided to stop living in fear and start enjoying life again. But peace doesn't last long. When a young man named Corey is accused of killing a boy he was babysitting, it sets off a chain of violence that pulls Laurie back into a nightmare she thought she had escaped. You'll find yourself watching a story that mixes slasher thrills with a slower, more personal look at trauma and how darkness can spread from one person to another. It's not just about Michael Myers anymore, and that shift might surprise you.

The acting is solid, especially Jamie Lee Curtis, who brings real weight to Laurie's journey. The pacing is uneven at times, with long stretches of drama between the scares, but when the action hits, it hits hard. Some fans might miss the nonstop Michael Myers action of earlier films, while others will appreciate the fresh direction. If you enjoy horror that takes its time and builds tension, this one is worth your evening.
endingExplained: In the final act, Corey fully embraces the darkness and becomes a new killer, even wearing Michael Myers' mask. Laurie and her granddaughter Allyson fight back, and Laurie finally kills Michael Myers for good, ending his reign of terror. Corey dies too, and Laurie destroys Michael's body in a trash compactor to make sure he never returns. The film ends with Laurie writing her memoir, finally at peace, having conquered the evil that haunted her for decades.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slasher horror with a dramatic twist.
